**Premise re-verified on merged `main` by the `domain:ui` seat — it holds, and the card is not stale.**

This card was serialized behind #6487 (PR #6495, merged 06:16Z) on the shared diagnostic seam rather than on a file. Since the upstream merge is the single most likely thing to have absorbed a downstream card, the premise was re-read on the merged ref rather than assumed:

- `SchemaRenderer.tsx:957` — `isDisabled` still calls `evaluator.evaluateCondition(...)` **bare on both legs**, no `onFault`, no reporter. Unchanged.
- `reportUnresolvableVisibilityPredicate` is **already imported in this very file** (line 34) and the reporting path is live at lines 674-679 and 701. The card's cost estimate is right: the remaining work really is local wiring plus the message-text decision.

**One correction to the card's own framing, in the direction that makes the asymmetry larger.** The body says the visibility chain sits "three lines above". On today's `main` it is not one chain of a few legs — **six** predicate legs route through `evaluateVisibilityPredicate` and therefore report:

`visibleWhen` (:875) · `visible` (:883) · `visibleOn` (:888) · `visibility` (:893) · `hidden` (:914) · `hiddenOn` (:917)

against **two** that do not: `disabled` and `disabledOn`. So the silent pair is not a straggler beside a neighbour — it is the only unreported pair in a file where every other declared-predicate leg is instrumented. The suggestion is unchanged and correct; the count is worth carrying because it is the argument for the card.

**Not dispatched yet — no capacity, not a doubt.** All five lane slots are occupied. This card is unblocked, unassigned, and first in line for the next free slot. The message-text question the card raises (`reportUnresolvableVisibilityPredicate`'s copy is written for a gate that did NOT bite, and here the safe default is the one that DOES) stays with the dev as a stop-and-report if it turns out to need a second reporter rather than a second message.

**Dispatched** by the `domain:ui` seat. Premise already re-verified on merged `main` in the comment above — read it before the body, it corrects the card's own framing upward (six instrumented legs against two silent, not "three lines above").

**You are the last of three.** Triage's family note names #6443 (app-shell), #6444 (core) and this card as one #6038 census. **Both siblings have landed** — #6443 at 04:5xZ, #6444 (PR #6492) at 06:16Z — so the fold-or-serial choice triage offered is moot and this is independent work. That is good news for scheduling and **bad news for your instrument**, which is the next point.

**⭐⭐ The hazard that will eat this card if you miss it: #6444 landed a dedupe on exactly your seam, hours ago.**

`packages/core/src/evaluator/ExpressionEvaluator.ts` now carries a module-level `warnedEvaluationFaults` set keyed by the site plus the fault source. Every fault report you add flows through it. So:

- **Prove the dedupe in BOTH directions, not one.** Same source ⇒ exactly one entry. **Different** sources ⇒ exactly two. Proving only the collapsing direction is compatible with a mechanism that collapses everything, and that reads as a pass.
- **Then audit the EXISTING suite in reverse.** #6444's own dev found a pre-existing test cell that reused the same fault source, and after the dedupe landed that cell would read the *previous* cell's entry and **pass while measuring nothing**. Your new reporting site is a fresh chance to create exactly that. Check whether any existing test that will now exercise the disabled path shares a fault source with another cell, and say what you found either way.

A test that cannot fail is worse here than no test, because this card exists precisely because a silent path went unnoticed.

**⛔ Add the diagnostic. Do NOT change the polarity.** `evaluateCondition` answering `true` for an unevaluable predicate — and therefore greying the control out — is existing behaviour, and the card describes it to explain why the silence matters, not to ask you to flip it. The neighbouring family landed with fail-soft **preserved deliberately**. Flipping it is a behaviour change on a shipped surface and needs a ruling this dispatch does not carry. If your measurements convince you the polarity is wrong, that is a **separate card** and a stop-and-report, not a rider.

**The message text is yours — triage said so explicitly**, and it is the real design content of this card:

> the message-text decision (this polarity's safe default BITES, so the visibility reporter's copy is wrong here) is the executing dev's, with the #3862/#3955 asymmetry analysis as the constraint

So `reportUnresolvableVisibilityPredicate`'s existing copy, written for a gate that did **not** bite, must not be reused verbatim for a gate that **does**. Write copy that is true for this polarity: the user is looking at a control they can see and cannot use, and the console line is the only thing that will ever tell them which predicate did it. ⛔ **One caveat**: if you find you need a second *reporter* rather than a second *message*, stop and report — a new exported reporter is a wider surface than this card was scoped for.

**Use #6038's seam, do not invent one.** `EvaluationOptions.onFault` hands back the fault the evaluator has **already caught**, at the same number of engine calls. ⛔ No `throwOnError`, no double evaluation. `reportUnresolvableVisibilityPredicate` is already imported in this very file at line 34, so the wiring is genuinely local — if your diff is reaching into other packages, something has gone wrong.

**Reverse verification.** Predict RED and observe it: make a `disabled` predicate unevaluable, show your assertion fails without the wiring and passes with it. Prove any mutation on disk rather than by an editor's exit code, and restore by hash against a pinned base SHA — ⛔ never against `origin/main`, which other worktrees move under you.

**Fence and hygiene.**
- Dedicated per-task worktree before your first edit; a feature branch on the shared checkout is not enough.
- ⛔ Never `git stash` — the stack lives in the common git directory, shared across every worktree, and a `pop` can restore another agent's work while reporting success.
- ⛔ Do not touch `content/docs/releases/`.
- Claim first: assign yourself, post a claim comment with your session ID and branch, re-read this thread before writing code.
- **Run tests narrowly.** The shared validation lock is a cross-agent resource; a wide run has been measured holding it nearly eighteen minutes. `packages/react` plus the pins that read this path is the right scope.

If you find something real outside this face, file it rather than widening the PR.
